project.name: System 1 (system1)
project.summary: The `decide` CLI and Agent Skills plugin that let coding agents in Claude Code, Codex and Pi hand closed judgements (yes/no, pick one, score) to a decision model (Jev on OpenRouter) and get typed, calibrated answers.

audiences.name: Agent user
audiences.description: A developer who installs the plugin in Claude Code, Codex or Pi and lets their agent call `decide`. M12 design partners are the first outside readers.

audiences.name: Script and CI author
audiences.description: Calls `decide` directly from CI, git hooks or scripts, branches on exit codes and parses the JSON envelope.

audiences.name: Maintainer
audiences.description: Works on this repo: the engine, CLI, generator, skills and release. Today that is the author and coding agents reading AGENTS.md.

sources.note: Names, version (0.3.1), npm scope, plugin description; source of every generated manifest.
Workspace scripts: check, generate, test:live, smoke, eval:routing, bench:startup, dev:link/unlink/status, release:check, release:publish.
Command dispatch and HELP text; entry.ts → bin.ts → main.ts, commands loaded lazily.
DECIDE_OPTIONS: every ask/many flag.
spec, config, usage, route, doctor, misc commands and their option tables.
EXIT and BY_CODE: exit code per error code.
json, jsonl and brief renderers.
Everything @garygentry/system1-core exports. Published, undocumented, stability undecided.

Tool definitions (TypeBox schemas in schemas.ts) and handlers: ask, many, spec-check, usage, route, doctor (DOCTOR_CHECKS). Result types ManyResult, AskResult, SpecCheckResult, UsageResult, DoctorResult.
DecisionsConfig keys and DEFAULTS: model, endpoint, concurrency 8, timeoutMs 5000, budget 200 calls / $0.05, egress.exclude, profiles, route. Layering user → repo → env.
Consent read and written only in <repo>/.system1/config.yaml.
Harness and session detection; innermost of CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CODEX_THREAD_ID, PI_SESSION_ID.

SpecSchema (version, description, questions, keep, sort, policy.thresholds{value,why}, source{glob,file,jsonl,diff,split}, examples[{id,state|file,expect}], provenance, meta); expect.ts expectation syntax; lookup dirs.
DEFAULT_EXCLUDES, scrubbing, size refusal; prepare() is the single path to the provider.
Source readers (glob, file, jsonl, diff, text, stdin) and splitters (file, hunk, row, lines:N, join).
Profiles (only typesafe/jev-1.13), answer types, undecided floor, response validation, OpenRouter transport with retries and timeout.
Decider: live, record, replay modes; fixture keys; replay miss as a typed error.
Budget projection and guard, concurrency pool, spend ledger (.system1/usage.jsonl), keep/sort projection.
BUILTIN_TRIGGERS, BUILTIN_IGNORE, route config merging (decision 0018).
Call order verified: prepare() (line 81) runs before checkBudget() (line 116).
End-to-end CLI behaviour, envelopes and exit codes, offline with injected fetch.
Config layering, egress, route, spec, doctor, decider behaviour.
Checks cli.md documents every command, flag and exit code, troubleshooting.md every doctor check and error code, and that links resolve. Does not check config keys or spec fields.
Six recipe specs with fixtures, replayed in pnpm test; meta.threshold_basis enforced.
Calibration sweep, labels and scoring behind docs/calibration.md.
Routing evals (--repeat N) and headless harness smoke tests; local only.
Emits plugin manifests, marketplaces, the bin/decide shim and hooks/claude-hooks.json; stamps versions.

pnpm dev:link | dev:unlink | dev:status: symlinks <claude config>/skills/system1 to plugins/system1 (system1@skills-dir); refuses anything it didn't make; reports what `claude plugin list --json` loads.
Generated shim: SYSTEM1_CLI override → checkout bundle → real install on PATH → pinned version via npx cache (SYSTEM1_NO_NPX stops a download). UserPromptSubmit hook runs `decide route --hook`.
ask (with references/), design, setup. Agent-facing; out of this plan's scope except for consistency.
pnpm check on Ubuntu and macOS × Node 22/24; packed job runs release:check (packed CLI, doctor and replayed decisions offline).
Decision records 0001–0018; 0006 superseded, 0002 and 0008 amended.
Milestones, Known gaps (routing, calibration scope, single model, macOS). § Architecture and § CLI contract are stale sketches.
M0–M8 records; M6 has the release procedure, M8 the onboarding walk.
Layout, rules, commands and verified harness notes for contributors.

documents.title: Lab: from zero to your first decisions
documents.purpose: A hands-on lab in Claude Code, in a throwaway repo: install, key, consent, then batch routing, a gated script, a negative case, spend, and repairing a bad spec, with a checkpoint per step.

outline.heading: Exercise 0: Make the lab repo
outline.intent: Download tools/evals/fixture-repo from main and git init it, so consent and specs stay per repo.

outline.heading: Exercise 1: Install the plugin
outline.intent: Marketplace install, /reload-plugins, `! decide version`; decide is on Claude's PATH, not the shell's.

outline.heading: Exercise 2: Add your key
outline.intent: Credentials file, mkdir and umask; never in the conversation.

outline.heading: Exercise 3: Run setup and grant consent
outline.intent: Doctor via the setup skill; `! decide config egress allow --confirm`; what is and is never sent.

outline.heading: Exercise 4: Route 300 tickets
outline.intent: Routing hint, ask skill, dry run, spend guard and approval; reading kept, undecided and confidence.

outline.heading: Exercise 5: Gate a risky script
outline.intent: Per-command verdicts; a badly posed question fixed by rewording, not overriding.

outline.heading: Exercise 6: When not to use it
outline.intent: An explain request stays with the agent.

outline.heading: Exercise 7: See what you spent
outline.intent: decide usage --session current, measured not estimated.

outline.heading: Exercise 8 (optional): Repair a bad question
outline.intent: The planted broken timeouts spec, repaired by the design skill, then spec check offline.

documents.verification: Exercises 2-8 walked in Claude Code 2.1.281 on 2026-09-24 with the plugin linked from a checkout; outputs are from those runs. Exercises 0-1 walked on 2026-09-24 against the published 0.3.2 in a fresh profile: the v0.3.2 tarball matches the checkpoint listing; the marketplace installs 0.3.2 at user scope; the hook is silent before the first decide call and hints after it; the first `decide version` fetched the CLI via npx in 3.7 s; doctor inside a session runs the npx-cached published CLI. tools/docs.test.ts checks the lab version, tag and tracked files.

documents.title: Run decide in CI, git hooks and scripts

outline.intent: `npm i -g @garygentry/system1`; no plugin needed.

outline.intent: Run `decide spec check` with committed fixtures and SYSTEM1_REPLAY=1: no key, no network, no consent.

outline.intent: Use --format json or jsonl with exit codes; branch on error.code, not the message.

outline.heading: Run live in CI
outline.intent: Key as a CI secret, consent committed as a deliberate team decision, spend guard left on.

outline.heading: A pre-commit gate
outline.intent: Judge the staged diff with `--diff --staged` and a spec, and use the answer only to add caution.

documents.verification: Replay-in-CI is what this repo's own CI does (cookbook test, release:check). No outside CI run exists yet, and there is no example workflow file for users. See gaps.

gaps.note: @garygentry/system1-core is published and the README calls it 'the engine as a library', but it has no documentation and no stability promise. Decided 2026-09-23: no library docs until M13's stability policy settles whether it is a supported API; M11 adds a minimal stability promise for the decider surface that adopted TypeScript imports (0019). Until then the README line may overstate it.

Command results have no published schema (`decide schema` covers inputs only), so output-reference must be derived from TS types and cannot be test-checked like cli.md. A `decide schema` for results, or a docs.test.ts check against the result types, would close this.

docs.test.ts now checks every DEFAULTS key in configuration.md and every SpecSchema property in spec-format.md, and link-checks docs/ subfolders. output.md has no such check, because results have no schema.
No outside user has run decide in their own CI or git hooks. The how-to rests on what this repo's CI does. M12 partners should confirm it.
The harnesses are unverified on macOS (ROADMAP gap 5). getting-started's install steps are verified on Linux only; CI covers the CLI alone on macOS.
ROADMAP § Architecture and § CLI contract are stale sketches. On 2026-09-23 they were marked historical and point to docs/architecture/, but they have not been rewritten.

Skills (plugins/system1/skills/*/SKILL.md and ask/references/) are agent-facing docs and outside this plan. spec-format, howto-spec and concepts restate some of their rules (question craft, thresholds). Nothing checks the two stay in step.

The calibration and threshold guidance rests on two TypeScript repos by one author, labelled by one AI labeller. choice and score questions are unmeasured (ROADMAP gap 3). Every page that recommends 0.3/0.5/0.7 inherits that scope.

Keep current file paths. README, the pages themselves and docs.test.ts's anchor checks link to docs/*.md and their headings. No doc-site exists, so any future site must keep these paths or redirect them.

Spec behaviour left as is after triage (2026-09-23). `policy.thresholds` is never read by the engine (`keep` filters), so the two can drift; that is by design, and spec-format says so. A spec's `source.file` takes no :START-END range, though an example's `file` does. What `provenance` should hold is unspecified. (Unknown nested keys are now refused.)

CLI behaviour left as is after triage (2026-09-23). Copying fixtures before .system1/fixtures/ exists puts them where lookups miss; that is how `cp -R` works, and specs.md warns about it. There is an import cycle: tools/doctor → ping → wiring → tools/context. (`spec check` now has `--strict`, exit 7; the dead bundled.ts is gone.)
The live-only steps were not run while drafting: recording a spec with --live, a live CI run, and a pre-commit hook that blocks a commit. The replay versions of each were run.
